To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have engineered and characterized a series of hyaluronic-acid (HA) based nanosystems that can be utilized for targeted delivery of siRNA to CD44 receptor overexpressing tumors.

we developed a series of CD 44 targeting HA-based nanoassemblies for siRNA delivery to tumor tissues and tumor initiating/stem cells, and that the nanosystems demonstrated target specific and potent gene silencing in solid tumors in vivo.
we developed a series of hyaluronic-acid based self-assembling nano-systems for targeted delivery of siRNA to solid tumors and metastases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, development and evaluation of novel HA based self-assembling nano-systems as siRNA delivery vehicles for CD44 target specific gene silencing in solid tumors and metastatic lesions.
the development of novel CD44 targeting nanosystems for siRNA delivery to CD44 overexpressed tumors.
developing and characterizing novel nanosystems that can deliver siRNAs into CD44 overexpresssing tumor cells and tissues for sequence specific gene silencing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have successfully developed and characterized HA based nano-assemblies as promising siRNA delivery systems that are capable of delivering siRNAs in a targeted manner to solid tumors and metastatic tumors.
the HA based nanosystem is capable of delivering siRNA into solid tumors in vivo, and is capable of target specific gene knock-down.
the HA-PEI nanosystems are promising siRNA delivery systems for targeted delivery of siRNA to solid tumors and metastatic lesions in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have engineered and characterized a novel class of CD44 targeting self-assembling nanocarriers for targeted delivery of siRNA to solid tumors.
the HA based nanosystem is a promising siRNA delivery vector for systemic targeting of cancers including tumor initiating cells and metastatic tumors.
we have successfully developed HA-based self-assembling nanocarriers that can encapsulate siRNAs, transfect into cells, and mediate target specific gene knock-down in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HA based self-assembling nanoassemblies could potentially be utilized for targeted siRNA therapy for solid tumors and metastatic lesions.
CD44 targeting nanosystems can be designed to deliver siRNAs to tumors and their metastasis.
the HA-derivatives could be used for targeted delivery of siRNA to tumors and metastatic lesions, which may be of interest for therapeutic applications.
